title: React Module 07 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of built-in Hooks, the Rules of Hooks, useState, useEffect, useContext, useRef, useMemo, useCallback, and useReducer.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What do Hooks let function components do?

options.text: Use React features such as state, effects, refs, and context

questions.explanation: Hooks are functions that let components use React features during rendering.

questions.prompt: Which are Rules of Hooks? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Call Hooks at the top level
Call Hooks only from React functions or custom Hooks
Call Hooks inside any loop if it is short
Use custom Hook names that start with `use`

questions.explanation: Stable Hook order matters, and custom Hook names signal Hook behavior to tooling.

questions.prompt: Which Hook is used for synchronizing with external systems after render?
questions.explanation: `useEffect` runs after render and is used for side effects such as subscriptions or data fetching.

questions.prompt: Which Hook reads a Context value?
questions.explanation: `useContext` reads the nearest matching provider value.

questions.prompt: What is a common use of `useRef`?

options.text: Accessing a DOM node or storing a mutable value that does not trigger renders

questions.explanation: Refs hold mutable `.current` values and can point to DOM elements. Updating a ref does not re-render.
`useMemo` caches a calculated value until dependencies change.
`useCallback(fn, deps)` returns a stable function reference while dependencies stay the same.

questions.prompt: When can `useReducer` be a good fit? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Updates are easier to express as actions
You need to perform network requests inside the reducer

questions.explanation: Reducers centralize pure state transitions. Side effects should stay outside reducers.
